instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Orders from the Shadows
cards.instruction: Hide that you set the problem in motion while quietly directing how everyone responds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The crates went to Leeds. Send the driver to me. Remember how I taught you to keep an incident report useful?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your email says Leeds. Shall I forward it to the manager?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good detective work. Now send only my corrected address. She needs a destination, not your entire investigation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She wants a timeline before she'll approve another van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start at 'Error discovered.' You used to bury the solution under the history. Send that for approval; I'll get a van quote while you write.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll rebuild the wedding bookings. Reassure the couples; you remember the customer calls I taught you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cancellation log has your initials.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you found the log. Now keep that screen turned away from the couples. Give them dates, not initials.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Restore-all emails them the canceller's name. If I re-enter by hand, they just get new confirmations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then by hand. You're finally checking before you click. I'll read out every date; use that careful typing I spent weeks getting out of you.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Not Up for Debate
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation from examining where your authority comes from or whether it is legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me down as shift leader. I taught you the café stock order; let's see tomorrow's milk total.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who put you in charge? I usually do that order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you're almost as quick at it as I was. How much milk?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order it, but I'm writing 'appointment unconfirmed' beside your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still filling the margins instead of doing the sums. Leave names off and give me quantities, like I taught you. Start with the milk.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: For Stability’s Sake
cards.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the director on the launch programme. I taught you the introductions: the department heads need someone above them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Her resignation's in the printer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've found it before they have. Good. Put it in my drawer; don't let them start fighting over her place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They think she's late. Each wants to do her opening speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll read it on her behalf. Give each head the same short introduction, like we practised. No extra adjectives for your favourite; none of them is taking her place tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the accounts out of the fair briefing. I taught you discretion; our chair can't lose everyone's confidence before we open.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She spent the stall money on that arch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've checked the figures. Now call it donated decoration, unless you want the stallholders replacing her at the gate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cover the shortfall if she signs an IOU.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sensible—you remembered paperwork. Get her signature privately after the welcome. Fold the IOU into your notebook, like I showed you; let them see a chair, not a debtor.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Name Your Backers
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal who supports their position, who authorized it, and who benefits from it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I send your workshop closure notice, name the people behind it. I taught you to put names against decisions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director approved it. Just send it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One name. A promising start. Who else backed closing us?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sales. They're getting our floor space, but don't put them in the notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You still leave out the people who gain. Add Sales, then tell me who approved giving them the space. I'm not sending a notice with half the names missing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This roof proposal says 'we recommend.' I taught you to name your sources. Who is 'we'?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finance backed the cheaper tiles. I need your signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better. Now who gave Finance the choice? Don't stop at the first name again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The facilities director. The savings pay for her office refurbishment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There, you've finally found the beneficiary. Put her name, her approval and her new office in the proposal. Then bring it back; I taught you to show all your working.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Strategic Retreat
cards.instruction: Describe every loss of control as a deliberate concession made from strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. I've graciously handed you the chess club chairmanship. You'll need room to develop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lost the vote. I need the cupboard key for tonight's match.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Of course. I'm releasing equipment control so you can practice responsibility.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And remove yourself as administrator. I can't change the fixtures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. I'll surrender my override too. You must learn to make decisions without my safety net.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've released the gallery from our exhibition. Remember what I taught you about leaving people room to grow?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They rejected us. Shall I collect the paintings?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, but say we're withdrawing them. You're still letting other people name your decisions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've already put everything outside. I'll get the van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've anticipated my next concession. We're giving them the pavement too. Load slowly; I taught you to make a withdrawal look gracious, not hurried.
